- A short runbook describing how you generate synthetic traffic for multi-tenant endpoints (shapes and scripting).
- Raw artifacts from representative runs (CSV of per-request latencies, server-side stdout logs, and the workbook that produced the P50/P95/P99 figures).
- A description of how you handle token-length variance and model-quantization variants in your test matrix.
- Any topology diagrams (replicas, proxies) used during the runs and the exact endpoint config (batching, KV cache settings).

We are under a calendar constraint this quarter; if possible can you deliver the artifacts by EOD Tuesday (6/3)? Also please point us to a sandbox where we can rerun a subset of tests.

From: rohan_mehta@redwood.example.com

Subject: Re: Atlas RFP - request for load test artifacts and methodology clarification

Sarah —

Thanks for the clear ask. We're attaching a concise evidence package (see attached workbook + CSVs) and a short narrative below explaining the methodology. High level:

- Test harness: We used our internal traffic generator (open-sourced harness available on request) to replay recorded arrival patterns and also to produce synthetic step-scaled sweeps. The harness emits per-request JSON lines and a consolidated CSV.
- Workloads: Two shapes were used — a production-inspired mixed-interactive shape (70% short chat, 30% long-completion) and a CPU-bound sampling shape (long-token tails for sampling-heavy clients).
- Warmup and priming: Each endpoint was primed with 10 minutes of low-rate traffic and then ramped for 20 minutes before measurement windows to allow KV cache and JIT warming.
- Metrics: P50/P95/P99 observed at the load balancer (end-to-end), backend GPU queue latency, and per-token emission times. We include the CSVs and the workbook that produced the summary stats.

Attachments included: Atlas_RFP_Benchmark_Evidence_v3.xlsx, step-scaling-results-20250602.csv, run-configs-20250602.tar.gz, endpoint-topology.png

I'll loop in Marissa for the numeric summary and Karthik for sandbox access.

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com

Subject: Re: Atlas RFP - request for load test artifacts and methodology clarification

Sarah — adding more specifics on the numbers and the test matrix so procurement has concrete evidence for the appendix. Numbers below are from the measurement window (after warmup) on the mixed-interactive shape, single-tenant equivalent endpoint in our Dedicated pool, model variant: redwood-7b-quant-a: 

- Steady-state at 120 qps sustained (90 concurrent streams): P50 = 56 ms, P95 = 112 ms, P99 = 240 ms.
- Step-scale sweep (120 -> 480 qps, 1-minute steps): we observe graceful CPU queue growth and no hard errors; tail degrades predictably (P99 at 480 qps = 720 ms) and the system tripped into a secondary replica fan-out at 350 qps per endpoint as designed.
- Cold-start penalties observed when we removed priming: initial 90 seconds P99 spikes to ~1.8s for rare large-context requests (~8k tokens).
- Quantization comparison: float16 baseline vs quant-a: latency delta is ~8–12% faster with quant-a at equivalent throughput; quality measured on prompt set A shows <0.6% top-line regression for generation tasks used in our evals.

Methodology notes (short):
- Traffic shaping: Poisson arrival overlayed with occasional 10% microbursts (100–300 ms injection) to simulate interactive jitter.
- Measurement windows: 5-minute steady windows after 20-minute ramp; we report median of three independent runs.
- Failure modes: all runs recorded 5xx at <0.01% at highest tested load; we include per-request error flags in the CSV.

Attached workbook has the pivot tables and raw samples. If procurement needs a condensed one-pager with the single-cause path to the SLA number, we can produce that by EOD.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Performance Engineer — Redwood Inference

Alan — thanks, we can do that. Plan and artifacts below: 

1) Token-length distribution: attached as a small CSV in the Drive link (percentiles: P10=12 tokens, P25=24, P50=48, P75=220, P90=512, P95=980, P99=3600). The distribution used in the mixed-interactive shape is biased toward short exchanges but includes a heavy tail to reflect real conversational clients.

2) Sandbox access: we've provisioned a one-time sandbox project with the same endpoint config. Steps: 
  - Open the Drive folder at https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAtlas-RFP-evidence and follow the sandbox-access-instructions.pdf (attached).
  - Request token via our secure ticketing link (we will issue a scoped API key valid for 48 hours).
  - Run the quick-start harness: ./harness/run_sweep.sh --config run-configs/atlas_rfp_mixed.json --duration 00:25:00 --output ./results 

3) Timeline: we'll issue the sandbox API key within 3 hours of your ticket; keys expire 48 hours after issue. We will also stand up a Zoom lab session tomorrow 09:00 PT if you'd like an operator from our side to run the sweep with you.

I have uploaded the token-distribution.csv, sandbox instructions, and a condensed one-page appendix draft to the Drive folder. If procurement needs a signed addendum allowing sandbox access, the DocuSign envelope (ATD-ADDENDUM) is live here: https://www.docusign.com/Envelope?ID=0A1B2C3D-ATD-ADDENDUM

—Karthik
